questions.stem: A technician removes the index pins from an oxygen cylinder yoke because a cylinder will not fit. What safety function has been defeated?
options: Pipeline pressure regulator
Scavenger interface
Prevention of mounting the wrong gas cylinder
Pipeline DISS connection
questions.explanation: The Pin Index Safety System uses gas-specific pin positions. Removing the pins defeats that protection and can permit the wrong cylinder to be attached.

questions.stem: A pipeline hose is being connected to the workstation. Which feature prevents an oxygen hose from being attached to a different medical-gas inlet?
options: Gas-specific DISS diameter and threading
Pin-index yoke pins
15/22-mm common gas outlet fitting
Flow-control knob shape
questions.explanation: DISS uses noninterchangeable gas-specific diameter and threading at pipeline connections.

questions.stem: A full oxygen cylinder enters the workstation at approximately 2200 psi. Which component FIRST reduces this variable high pressure to approximately 45 psi?
options: First-stage pressure regulator
Flow-control valve
Pipeline inlet check valve
Common gas outlet
questions.explanation: The first-stage cylinder regulator converts variable high cylinder pressure to a constant lower output near 45 psi.

questions.stem: At very low fresh gas flow through a Thorpe tube, a replacement flowmeter calibrated for a gas with different physical properties is installed. Which property most affects accuracy in this low-flow range?
options: Density
Viscosity
Vapor pressure
Critical temperature
questions.explanation: Low flow is predominantly laminar, so viscosity is the important gas property.

questions.stem: At high flow through a Thorpe tube, which gas property becomes the dominant determinant of flow?
options: Viscosity
Vapor pressure
Critical temperature
Density
questions.explanation: At high turbulent flow, density becomes the dominant gas property.

questions.stem: A leak develops in a flowmeter tube upstream from the oxygen flowmeter. Which design feature most directly decreases the chance of delivering a hypoxic mixture?
options: The common gas outlet has a 22-mm outer diameter
The oxygen cylinder regulator outputs 45 psi
The hanger yoke contains a filter
Oxygen is positioned downstream of the other flowmeters
questions.explanation: Downstream oxygen placement helps preserve oxygen delivery if an upstream flowmeter leaks.

questions.stem: Oxygen and nitrous oxide are linked by the workstation proportioning system. Air is then added to the fresh gas mixture. Which statement is most accurate?
options: The system guarantees at least 25% oxygen regardless of all gases used
The proportioning system directly measures final inspired oxygen concentration
A hypoxic mixture can still occur because the proportioning system governs only oxygen and nitrous oxide
Adding air disables nitrous oxide delivery completely
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes that the proportioning system only links oxygen and nitrous oxide and does not guarantee a safe final oxygen concentration when other gases are added.

questions.stem: A machine with a common-gas-outlet check valve is being tested for a low-pressure leak. Which test principle is required?
options: Apply negative pressure to the low-pressure system
Pressurize the cylinder above pipeline pressure
Close the scavenger relief ports
Apply only positive pressure at the common gas outlet
questions.explanation: The lecture states that machines with outlet check valves require negative-pressure testing for low-pressure leaks.

questions.stem: Which TWO fittings are correct for the workstation common gas outlet? (Select 2)
options: 22-mm female internal fitting
30-mm female fitting
22-mm male external fitting
15-mm male external fitting
15-mm female internal fitting
19-mm male fitting
questions.explanation: The common gas outlet is 15-mm female internally and 22-mm male externally; 19- and 30-mm conical fittings are reserved for scavenging.

questions.stem: A provider is rushed, distracted by conversation, and skips part of the machine check. Which concept from the lecture BEST characterizes the resulting risk?
options: Anesthesia adverse events are often multifactorial and strongly influenced by human factors
Modern workstations eliminate most human-factor risk
Equipment failures are usually isolated from provider behavior
Only technical failures are relevant to machine-related events
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes multifactorial events and human contributors including distraction, haste, fatigue, and unfamiliarity.

questions.stem: Which THREE human factors are specifically emphasized as aggravating contributors to anesthesia adverse events? (Select 3)
options: Fatigue
Haste
Equipment standardization
Pipeline pressure
DISS indexing
Inattention/distraction
questions.explanation: Inattention/distraction, haste, and fatigue are specifically discussed as aggravating factors.

questions.stem: A spontaneously breathing intubated patient is transported using a Mapleson A system. Minute ventilation is 8 L/min. What is the minimum fresh gas flow identified by this lecture?
options: Approximately 8 L/min
Approximately 5.6 L/min
Approximately 16 L/min
Approximately 2 L/min
questions.explanation: Mapleson A requires fresh gas flow of at least 0.7 × minute ventilation: 0.7 × 8 = 5.6 L/min.

questions.stem: A Mapleson B/C-type system is used for transport. Minute ventilation is 8 L/min. Which fresh gas flow range best matches the lecture?
options: Approximately 24–32 L/min
Approximately 5.6–8 L/min
Approximately 12–20 L/min
Approximately 4–6 L/min
questions.explanation: The lecture gives 1.5–2.5 × minute ventilation for Mapleson B/C: 12–20 L/min when minute ventilation is 8 L/min.

questions.stem: A freestanding PEEP valve is added to an older transport circuit. Immediately afterward ventilation becomes difficult. What should be checked FIRST?
options: Whether the DISS connector is color coded
Whether the oxygen cylinder pressure is exactly 2200 psi
Whether the PEEP connector itself was positioned incorrectly and obstructed flow
Whether the vaporizer was filled
questions.explanation: The lecture warns that an incorrectly placed freestanding PEEP connector can itself obstruct the breathing system.

questions.stem: During neck surgery, the patient's face and airway connections are hidden beneath drapes. Delivered ventilation suddenly falls. Which equipment problem deserves immediate consideration?
options: The oxygen flowmeter has moved downstream
Breathing-circuit or endotracheal-tube connection has become disconnected
Grounded equipment
Discard the tube and drapes immediately
questions.explanation: The lecture highlights circuit disconnection during neck surgery because drapes can hide the airway and ET-tube connection.

questions.stem: A vaporizer is tipped while being moved between machines. Why should it not simply be returned upright and used?
options: Tipping can alter agent delivery and expose the patient to excessive anesthetic
Tipping disables the DISS connector
Tipping converts AC current to DC current
Tipping permanently closes the APL valve
questions.explanation: The lecture specifically warns that tipping a vaporizer can increase anesthetic dose to the patient.

questions.stem: The operating room loses main electrical power. Which TWO preparations are emphasized while workstation battery power remains? (Select 2)
options: Open the backup cylinder and leave the pipeline connected
Set up an alternative ventilation method such as a Mapleson system
Disable alarms to conserve battery
Increase reliance on electrically powered equipment
Continue unchanged until battery depletion
Prepare an intravenous anesthetic technique if gas delivery becomes unavailable
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends using the limited battery interval to prepare alternative ventilation and IV anesthesia such as propofol/TIVA.

questions.stem: A workstation loses wall power. Before deciding how long normal anesthesia can continue, what information is MOST important to know?
options: Total cylinder pressure
Whether the OR is isolated power
Which machine functions actually operate on its backup battery
The common gas outlet diameter
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes that machines differ in what remains powered; providers should know which monitors, alarms, and ventilator functions are battery-supported.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes the electrical safety configuration presented for the operating room?
options: Equipment is grounded while the OR power supply is ungrounded
Both equipment and power supply are grounded exactly as in a home
Only the anesthesia workstation is ungrounded
Neither equipment nor power supply is grounded
questions.explanation: The lecture describes OR power as ungrounded while equipment is grounded.

questions.stem: An electrosurgical return pad has only partial contact with the patient's skin. Which complication is the primary concern?
options: Hypercarbia from increased apparatus dead space
Hypoxic mixture from flowmeter leakage
Patient burn from concentrated current density at the poor-contact area
Cylinder transfilling through the yoke
questions.explanation: Poor return-pad contact can concentrate current and cause thermal injury.

questions.stem: Which THREE elements must coexist for an operating-room fire? (Select 3)
options: Scavenging suction
Ignition source
Pipeline pressure
Oxidizer
Electrical grounding
Fuel
questions.explanation: The classic fire triangle consists of ignition, oxidizer, and fuel.

questions.stem: During facial surgery under nasal-cannula oxygen, electrocautery will be used near the airway. Which intervention BEST reduces fire risk?
options: Increase FiO2 immediately before cautery
Use the lowest tolerated FiO2 and prevent oxygen accumulation beneath the drapes
Use the lowest FiO2 tolerated during open oxygen delivery near the airway
Seal the drapes tightly around the cannula to retain oxygen
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends allowing prep to dry, avoiding oxygen pooling, and using the lowest FiO2 tolerated during open oxygen delivery near the surgical field.

questions.stem: Which THREE actions are appropriate fire-prevention measures from the lecture? (Select 3)
options: Keep drapes elevated to reduce oxygen pooling
Use the lowest tolerated FiO2 and prevent oxygen accumulation beneath the drapes
Use the lowest FiO2 tolerated during open oxygen delivery near the airway
Allow skin preparation solution to dry before draping
Increase oxygen flow before electrocautery
Cover wet prep immediately with occlusive drapes
questions.explanation: Dry prep, prevention of oxygen pooling, and minimizing FiO2 as tolerated are emphasized prevention measures.

questions.stem: During airway surgery, the provider hears a pop and sees a flash at the endotracheal tube. What should occur FIRST?
options: Close the APL valve before disconnecting anything
Leave the tube in place and pour saline through the connector
Increase fresh gas flow to wash smoke from the circuit
Remove the tube and stop gas flow simultaneously
questions.explanation: A pop, flash, or smoke can indicate fire. For an airway fire, the lecture emphasizes removing the tube and stopping gas flow simultaneously.

questions.stem: After the burning endotracheal tube is removed and gas flow is stopped, what is the most appropriate NEXT action from the lecture sequence?
options: Reconnect the original circuit before assessing injury
Restart oxygen at 100% before inspecting the airway
Discard the tube and drapes immediately
Pour saline into the airway and remove burning material
questions.explanation: After stopping gases and removing the tube, saline is used to extinguish residual fire and burning material is removed before ventilation and airway reassessment.

questions.stem: A drape fire occurs on the patient's chest without airway involvement. Which sequence BEST matches the lecture?
options: Extinguish → continue surgery → stop gases after closure
Stop gases → remove burning drapes/material → extinguish → assess patient
Assess patient → increase oxygen → remove drapes → extinguish
Remove monitors → evacuate → leave burning material in place
questions.explanation: The lecture's patient-fire sequence is stop gases, remove burning material, extinguish, then assess the patient.

questions.stem: During electrosurgery, alcohol-based prep has not fully dried and supplemental oxygen is pooling under the drapes. Which elements of the fire triangle are being increased?
options: Resistance and capacitance
Pressure and current
Fuel and oxidizer
Ignition and grounding
questions.explanation: Wet/flammable prep contributes fuel and pooled oxygen increases the oxidizer component; electrocautery can provide ignition.

questions.stem: A fire occurs and is extinguished without obvious patient injury. Which statement BEST reflects the lecture's risk-management approach?
options: Discard the tube and drapes immediately
Discard involved equipment if the patient is stable
Document only if the patient sustained an injury
Preserve the scene and notify risk management even if immediate injury appears absent
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes preserving the scene, notifying the hospital risk manager, and following reporting requirements after a fire event.

questions.stem: During induction, the hospital oxygen pipeline becomes contaminated. The reserve E-cylinder is full and already open, but the pipeline remains connected. What is the BEST immediate workstation action?
options: Activate the oxygen flush continuously
Close the cylinder and increase air flow
Disconnect the oxygen pipeline immediately regardless of its status
Disconnect the oxygen pipeline from the machine
questions.explanation: Pipeline oxygen is normally 50–55 psi while cylinder gas is regulated to about 40–45 psi. The pipeline must be disconnected to ensure use of the cylinder when the pipeline source is contaminated.

questions.stem: A provider completes the morning machine check and leaves the oxygen E-cylinder open. Several hours later the central oxygen pipeline fails. What hazard does this practice create?
options: Pressurize the cylinder above pipeline pressure
The cylinder regulator will raise pipeline pressure above 55 psi
The reserve cylinder may be depleted before the pipeline failure is recognized
The common gas outlet will automatically vent cylinder oxygen
questions.explanation: Leaving the cylinder open can allow it to supply gas after pipeline failure, potentially depleting the reserve before the provider recognizes the failure. The lecture recommends closing it after checking pressure.

questions.stem: A workstation receives pipeline oxygen at 52 psi and regulated cylinder oxygen at 45 psi. Both sources are connected. Which source should supply the machine under normal conditions?
options: Cylinder oxygen until pressure falls below 45 psi
Cylinder oxygen because cylinder gas has priority
Pipeline oxygen because its pressure is higher
High pipeline pressure
questions.explanation: The deliberate pressure difference causes preferential use of pipeline gas.

questions.stem: Which findings should a proper pre-use machine check identify before they produce hypoxemia? (Select 3)
options: Disconnected gas hose
Absent backup oxygen reserve
Unattached or unopened oxygen cylinder
Charged backup battery
Normal downstream oxygen flowmeter position
Open the reserve oxygen cylinder for the entire case
questions.explanation: The lecture specifically lists disconnected hoses, absent backup oxygen, and cylinder problems among hypoxemia hazards that a proper check should catch.

questions.stem: The workstation repeatedly fails the breathing-circuit leak check despite reseating visible connections. What is the most appropriate NEXT step emphasized in the lecture?
options: Close the APL valve and increase pipeline pressure
Open the reserve oxygen cylinder for the entire case
Replace the breathing circuit and repeat the check
Disable the leak alarm and proceed
questions.explanation: The instructor specifically notes that swapping the circuit often resolves a persistent breathing-circuit leak.

questions.stem: After intubation, bilateral breath sounds and end-tidal carbon dioxide are confirmed. Five minutes later carbon dioxide is progressively rising and the patient is not breathing spontaneously. What should be checked FIRST?
options: Whether the vaporizer interlock is engaged
Whether the oxygen cylinder was closed after the machine check
Whether mechanical ventilation was started
Whether the pipeline pressure exceeds cylinder pressure
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies forgetting to turn on the ventilator after intubation as the most common delivery-system cause of hypercarbia in this scenario.

questions.stem: A mechanically ventilated patient develops progressive hypercarbia. Which THREE workstation/circuit problems from the lecture can cause this finding? (Select 3)
options: Exhausted carbon dioxide absorbent
Added apparatus dead space
Hypercarbia from increased apparatus dead space
Increased apparatus dead space
Correctly functioning unidirectional valve
Incompetent unidirectional valve
questions.explanation: Exhausted absorbent, incompetent valves, and added dead space can all increase inspired/rebreathed carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: A patient develops hypercarbia after several tubing extensions are added between the Y-piece and airway. The ventilator is functioning and the absorbent is fresh. Which mechanism BEST explains the change?
options: Increased apparatus dead space
The change proves the ventilator is functioning normally
The color change confirms the absorbent is fresh
Added apparatus dead space
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies tubing extensions and added dead space as a cause of hypercarbia.

questions.stem: During manual ventilation immediately after induction, airway pressure rapidly rises and the reservoir bag becomes very tense. The circuit is not kinked. Which error should be suspected FIRST?
options: Reserve oxygen cylinder left closed
Open the APL valve and discontinue all ventilation
APL valve left closed
Tipping permanently closes the APL valve
questions.explanation: An APL valve left closed after induction can cause excessive breathing-system pressure.

questions.stem: After replacing a breathing circuit, no gas reaches the patient despite normal machine pressures. Inspection reveals no kink. Which overlooked setup error from the lecture is most likely?
options: Replace the breathing circuit and repeat the check
Plastic wrapping remains over a circuit connector
Increase fresh gas flow to wash smoke from the circuit
Disconnect the oxygen pipeline from the machine
questions.explanation: Unremoved plastic wrapping can occlude a connector and should be detected during the machine check.

questions.stem: Which TWO features of the hanger-yoke assembly directly reduce gas-delivery hazards? (Select 2)
options: Gas-tight seal at the cylinder connection
Incompetent unidirectional valve
Prevention of mounting the wrong gas cylinder
Unidirectional flow/check-valve function
Correctly functioning unidirectional valve
Flow-control needle valve
questions.explanation: The hanger yoke provides a gas-tight seal and contains a unidirectional valve that reduces leakage/backflow hazards.

questions.stem: A flowmeter bank is damaged upstream from the oxygen tube. Which arrangement provides the safest gas path?
options: Oxygen tube positioned furthest downstream
Oxygen tube positioned furthest upstream
All tubes positioned in parallel with no downstream order
Nitrous oxide tube downstream of oxygen
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes downstream oxygen placement to reduce hypoxic-mixture risk from upstream leaks.

questions.stem: A clinician assumes the oxygen–nitrous proportioning linkage guarantees a safe inspired oxygen concentration. Which scenario disproves that assumption?
options: Closing the reserve cylinder increases nitrous oxide concentration
Adding another gas such as helium can still permit oxygen concentration below 21%
Oxygen proportioning linkage
Automatic oxygen concentration analysis
questions.explanation: The proportioning system does not protect against every gas combination; the lecture specifically warns about additional gases such as helium or air.

questions.stem: A machine without a common-gas-outlet check valve is evaluated for a low-pressure leak. Which general test direction is supported by the lecture?
options: Cylinder pressure must be increased above 2200 psi
The scavenging system must be occluded
Positive pressure can be applied at the common gas outlet
Only negative pressure can detect the leak
questions.explanation: The lecture contrasts machines without an outlet check valve, which can be tested with positive pressure, with machines having a check valve, which require negative pressure.

questions.stem: A patient is being ventilated with a transport circuit that permits rebreathing if fresh gas flow is inadequate. Which strategy from the lecture is safest for Mapleson B/C systems?
options: Prevention of mounting the wrong gas cylinder
Reduce flow below minute ventilation to conserve oxygen
Close the APL valve completely
Run high fresh gas flow within the required multiple of minute ventilation
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends high flow for Mapleson B/C because they require approximately 1.5–2.5 times minute ventilation.

questions.stem: A machine check is delegated to an anesthesia technician. What responsibility remains with the anesthesia provider according to the lecture?
options: Confirm that the machine check was actually completed
Leave the reserve cylinder open to prove the check occurred
Bypass the circuit leak test if the technician signed the room sheet
Assume delegation eliminates the need to verify readiness
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly says to confirm the morning machine check was actually completed even when delegated.

questions.stem: Which TWO breathing-system assembly errors from the lecture can contribute to hypercarbia? (Select 2)
options: Increase electrocautery output to test the isolated power system
Equipment grounded in the OR
Hoses connected to incorrect outlets or inlets
Apply negative pressure to the low-pressure system
Place the reservoir bag between the patient and unidirectional valves
Reservoir bag positioned incorrectly relative to inspiratory/expiratory valves
questions.explanation: The lecture advises confirming hoses are on the correct outlets/inlets and that the reservoir bag is not incorrectly positioned in the valve pathway.

questions.stem: A provider sees a color change in the carbon dioxide absorbent during a case with rising carbon dioxide. Which interpretation is most appropriate based on the lecture?
options: The color change confirms the absorbent is fresh
The change proves the ventilator is functioning normally
The absorbent may be exhausted and should be considered as a source of rebreathing
The change indicates pipeline oxygen contamination
questions.explanation: The lecture specifically says to watch for the absorbent color change as a clue to exhaustion in hypercarbia troubleshooting.

questions.stem: A workstation power failure occurs during volatile anesthesia. The backup battery is expected to last roughly 40 minutes on this machine. What is the BEST planning principle?
options: Transition to a sustainable alternative well before battery depletion
Charged backup battery
Use the full 40 minutes before preparing an alternative
Only the anesthesia workstation is ungrounded
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes using the battery window to establish an alternative and having the patient safely covered before battery power is exhausted.

questions.stem: an operating-room fire has been extinguished. Which action is most appropriate for subsequent risk investigation?
options: Discard the tube and drapes immediately
Clean and return the circuit to service
Preserve the ET tube, circuit, drapes, and other involved equipment
Document only if the patient sustained an injury
questions.explanation: The lecture instructs providers to preserve the scene and equipment and follow institutional/regulatory reporting procedures.

questions.stem: During a room fire that cannot be extinguished promptly, which action becomes appropriate according to the lecture?
options: Activate the fire alarm and consider evacuation
Continue the procedure until the battery fails
Leave all drapes on the patient during evacuation
Disable the leak alarm and proceed
questions.explanation: The lecture notes that failure to extinguish the fire should prompt alarm activation and consideration of evacuation.

questions.stem: Which finding BEST distinguishes a cylinder-supply safety feature from a pipeline-supply safety feature?
options: Both systems regulate cylinder pressure to 45 psi
DISS controls cylinders while PISS controls wall hoses
PISS uses pin positions at the cylinder yoke, whereas DISS uses gas-specific diameter/threading at pipeline connections
Cylinder transfilling through the yoke
questions.explanation: PISS is the cylinder-yoke indexing system; DISS is the noninterchangeable pipeline connector system.

questions.stem: Wall O2 is 52 psi and cylinder O2 is regulated to 45 psi. Which source supplies the machine first?
options: Whichever was opened last
Both equally
Pipeline O2
Cylinder O2
questions.explanation: Pipeline pressure is intentionally higher, so the machine preferentially draws from the pipeline.

questions.stem: You need cylinder O2 because the hospital O2 supply is contaminated. What must you do?
options: Increase cylinder pressure
Disconnect the pipeline
Open the APL valve
Close the cylinder
questions.explanation: The pipeline must be disconnected or its higher pressure will remain the preferred source.

questions.stem: Why is the O2 cylinder closed after its pressure is checked?
options: To preserve reserve O2 and reveal pipeline failure
To test the DISS fitting
To raise pipeline pressure
To prevent vaporizer back pressure
questions.explanation: Closing the cylinder preserves the reserve and allows a pipeline failure to become apparent before the cylinder is depleted.

questions.stem: Which region is downstream of the first-stage regulator but upstream of the flow-control valves?
options: Low-pressure system
High-pressure system
Intermediate-pressure system
Scavenging system
questions.explanation: The intermediate-pressure system lies between the first-stage regulator and the flow-control valves.

questions.stem: Which region begins downstream of the flow-control valves?
options: Cylinder-supply system
High-pressure system
Low-pressure system
Intermediate-pressure system
questions.explanation: The lecture defines the low-pressure system as all components downstream of the flow-control valves.

questions.stem: A pipeline hose cannot fit the wrong gas inlet because of which system?
options: APL
CGO
PISS
DISS
questions.explanation: DISS uses gas-specific diameters and threading for pipeline connections.

questions.stem: Removing the index pins from a cylinder yoke creates what hazard?
options: Pipeline cross-connection
Excessive scavenging
Wrong cylinder attachment
Vaporizer overfilling
questions.explanation: Removing the pins bypasses PISS and can allow the wrong gas cylinder to be mounted.

questions.stem: A Bourdon gauge senses pressure by movement of what component?
options: Tapered glass tube
Solenoid valve
Flexible reservoir bag
Coiled metal tube
questions.explanation: Pressure straightens the coiled Bourdon tube and moves the gauge pointer.

questions.stem: Which hanger-yoke feature permits cylinder replacement while the machine remains in use?
options: Pressure-relief valve
Oxygen analyzer
Unidirectional valve
Flow-control valve
questions.explanation: The unidirectional valve reduces leakage from an empty yoke and permits cylinder replacement during use.

questions.stem: The pipeline is disconnected and the O2 cylinder is open. Gas is heard escaping from the pipeline inlet. Which failure best explains this?
options: Pipeline inlet check valve stuck open
Cylinder yoke check valve stuck closed
First-stage regulator set above 55 psi
DISS fitting preventing reverse flow
questions.explanation: With the pipeline absent, the inlet check valve should prevent cylinder gas from escaping backward through the pipeline connection. A stuck-open valve permits that loss.

questions.stem: Two O2 cylinders are mounted on a dual yoke. One is full and one is nearly empty. Which component limits transfilling from the full cylinder into the low-pressure cylinder?
options: Yoke check valve
First-stage regulator
Flow-control valve
Common gas outlet check valve
questions.explanation: The unidirectional check valve at each yoke limits reverse flow and transfilling between cylinders.

questions.stem: An O2 cylinder is opened during the morning check and then left open with normal pipeline pressure. Why is this unsafe?
options: A later pipeline failure may be masked while the cylinder silently empties
Cylinder pressure will raise pipeline pressure above 55 psi
The proportioning system will disable N2O
The flowmeter will read cylinder pressure instead of flow
questions.explanation: The cylinder should be checked and then closed. If left open, it can supply the machine during pipeline failure and be depleted before the provider recognizes the problem.

questions.stem: After hospital pipeline maintenance, the O2 pipeline gauge reads 52 psi, but the inspired O2 concentration falls despite 100% O2 selected. What is the FIRST corrective sequence?
options: Open the O2 cylinder, disconnect the pipeline, then verify inspired O2
Increase O2 flow and wait for the fail-safe
Open the O2 cylinder but leave the pipeline connected
Close the cylinder and use the O2 flush repeatedly
questions.explanation: Normal pressure does not exclude pipeline contamination. Because pipeline pressure exceeds regulated cylinder pressure, the contaminated pipeline must be disconnected so the cylinder becomes the source.

questions.stem: Pipeline O2 is 52 psi and the backup cylinder is open at a regulated 45 psi. Which source does the workstation preferentially use?
options: Pipeline O2 because its pressure is higher
Cylinder O2 because it is physically closer
Both equally because the regulator equalizes them
Whichever source was opened first
questions.explanation: Pipeline pressure is intentionally higher than regulated cylinder pressure, so the machine preferentially uses the pipeline while it remains pressurized.

questions.stem: A flowmeter is accurate at low flow but increasingly inaccurate at high flow after the wrong gas-specific tube is installed. Which property now matters most?
options: Density
Viscosity
Critical temperature
Vapor pressure
questions.explanation: High flow is predominantly turbulent, making density the important gas property. Low laminar flow is more dependent on viscosity.

questions.stem: A leak develops in a flowmeter tube positioned upstream from O2. Which statements are correct? Select 2.
options: Downstream O2 placement reduces the chance of a hypoxic mixture
The O2 analyzer remains necessary because the design is not fail-proof
The proportioning system detects every downstream leak
Moving O2 upstream would make the arrangement safer
The fail-safe closes whenever a flowmeter tube leaks
The leak cannot affect delivered gas composition
questions.explanation: Placing O2 downstream protects against loss through an upstream tube leak, but only an O2 analyzer verifies the final delivered oxygen concentration.

questions.stem: O2 and N2O are mechanically proportioned, but another gas is added. The final mixture becomes hypoxic. Why did the proportioning system not prevent it?
options: It links O2 and N2O flows rather than measuring final inspired O2
It functions only when cylinder O2 is used
It is bypassed whenever total flow exceeds 5 L/min
It responds only to common gas outlet pressure
questions.explanation: The proportioning system governs the O2:N2O relationship. It does not directly measure final inspired oxygen and cannot prevent every hypoxic mixture involving other gases.

questions.stem: O2 supply pressure falls enough to activate the pressure-sensor shutoff. Which statement is most accurate?
options: N2O is reduced or interrupted, but a safe final O2 concentration is not guaranteed
All fresh gas flow stops immediately
The device measures inspired O2 and adds O2 automatically
Air is shut off before N2O
questions.explanation: The pressure-sensor shutoff responds to O2 supply pressure by reducing or stopping N2O. It does not analyze the final gas mixture.

questions.stem: A low-pressure leak test is attempted with positive pressure at the common gas outlet, but the workstation has an outlet check valve. Why can the test miss a leak?
options: The check valve can block transmitted positive pressure, so negative-pressure testing is required
Positive pressure closes every vaporizer automatically
The test evaluates only the high-pressure system
The check valve vents test pressure into scavenging
questions.explanation: With a common-gas-outlet check valve, positive pressure may not adequately test the upstream low-pressure system. The lecture specifies a negative-pressure test.

questions.stem: Which common gas outlet fittings match the lecture? Select 2.
options: 15-mm female internal fitting
22-mm male external fitting
19-mm male scavenging fitting
30-mm female scavenging fitting
15-mm male internal fitting
22-mm female external fitting
questions.explanation: The common gas outlet is 15 mm female internally and 22 mm male externally. The 19- and 30-mm fittings are associated with scavenging.

questions.stem: A provider is unfamiliar with a workstation, is rushing, and skips part of the pre-use check. Which interpretation best matches the lecture?
options: Human factors can combine with equipment and system problems to produce an adverse event
Modern workstations make skipped checks clinically unimportant
Only technical failure counts as an equipment-related adverse event
The risk is limited to the induction period
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes that adverse events are often multifactorial, combining human factors, system problems, and technical failures.

questions.stem: Which conditions increase the chance that a provider-related error contributes to an equipment event? Select 3.
options: Fatigue
Haste
Distraction
Downstream O2 placement
DISS indexing
A charged backup battery
questions.explanation: Fatigue, haste, and inattention/distraction are specifically emphasized human contributors.

questions.stem: The machine repeatedly fails its breathing-circuit leak check. Connections appear secure. What is the most efficient next step emphasized in the lecture?
options: Replace the breathing circuit and repeat the check
Increase pipeline pressure
Close the APL valve and begin the case
Open the backup O2 cylinder
questions.explanation: Breathing-circuit leaks are common, and the lecture notes that swapping the circuit often resolves a persistent failed leak check.

questions.stem: After intubation, breath sounds and ETCO2 initially confirm placement. ETCO2 then rises steadily and the patient is apneic. What should be checked FIRST?
options: Whether the ventilator was actually started
Whether the vaporizer was tipped
Whether the O2 cylinder is full
Whether the Bovie return pad is attached
questions.explanation: The lecture highlights failure to turn on the ventilator after intubation as a common delivery-system cause of hypercarbia.

questions.stem: ETCO2 is rising and inspired CO2 is also above zero. Which equipment causes fit this pattern? Select 3.
options: Exhausted CO2 absorbent
Incompetent unidirectional valve
Added apparatus dead space
Isolated pipeline O2 failure
Poor electrosurgical pad contact
A fully charged battery
questions.explanation: Rebreathing and apparatus dead space can cause delivery-system hypercarbia. Exhausted absorbent and incompetent valves are classic rebreathing causes.

questions.stem: A spontaneously breathing patient has a minute ventilation of 10 L/min on a Mapleson A circuit. Which fresh gas flow meets the lecture's minimum?
options: 7 L/min
5 L/min
10 L/min
15 L/min
questions.explanation: For spontaneous ventilation with Mapleson A, the lecture gives a minimum FGF of about 0.7 × minute ventilation: 7 L/min.

questions.stem: A Mapleson B/C circuit is used with minute ventilation 8 L/min. Which fresh gas flow range best limits rebreathing?
options: 12–20 L/min
5.6–8 L/min
4–6 L/min
24–32 L/min
questions.explanation: The lecture gives approximately 1.5–2.5 × minute ventilation for Mapleson B/C systems: 12–20 L/min here.

questions.stem: A new breathing circuit passes visual inspection, but no gas reaches the patient. The tubing is not kinked. What overlooked setup error should be checked next?
options: Plastic packaging left across a connector
A fully charged backup battery
The cylinder color code
The electrosurgical return pad
questions.explanation: The lecture specifically warns that leftover plastic wrap can occlude a breathing-circuit connector.

questions.stem: Immediately after switching from manual ventilation, circuit pressure becomes dangerously high. Which setup error is most consistent with the lecture?
options: APL valve left closed
O2 cylinder left closed
CGO check valve present
Scavenger reservoir bag partially filled
questions.explanation: An APL valve left closed after induction can produce excessive breathing-system pressure.

questions.stem: During neck surgery, delivered tidal volume suddenly falls while the airway is hidden under drapes. What should be checked immediately?
options: ETT and breathing-circuit connections
Cylinder pin index
Vaporizer fill port
Electrosurgical grounding pad
questions.explanation: The lecture highlights hidden circuit or ETT disconnection during neck surgery because drapes obscure the airway connections.

questions.stem: A vaporizer was moved between rooms and briefly tipped. Soon after induction, agent concentration is unexpectedly high. What is the best explanation?
options: Tipping altered vaporizer delivery and can cause excessive agent output
The DISS connection changed vaporizer pressure
The O2 proportioner increased agent concentration
The scavenger pulled liquid agent into the circuit
questions.explanation: The lecture warns that tipping a vaporizer can increase anesthetic delivery.

questions.stem: Main electrical power fails. The workstation reports about 40 minutes of battery remaining. What should that number mean clinically?
options: A limited window to establish a safe alternative plan, not permission to continue unchanged
All workstation functions are guaranteed for exactly 40 minutes
Gas delivery will stop immediately despite the battery
The ventilator is guaranteed to outlast every monitor
questions.explanation: Typical battery duration is limited and machine-specific. The lecture frames it as time to prepare alternative ventilation and anesthetic delivery.

questions.stem: Two workstation models both have charged batteries, but one loses its ventilator during a power failure. What lesson from the lecture explains the difference?
options: Providers must know which specific functions each machine supports on battery
Battery power depends on pipeline pressure
DISS configuration determines battery-supported functions
The common gas outlet controls electrical backup
questions.explanation: Battery-supported monitors, alarms, and ventilator functions vary by workstation, so the provider must know the specific machine.

questions.stem: A device draws 2 A from a 120-V source. What electrical power is being used?
questions.explanation: Power equals voltage × current: 120 V × 2 A = 240 W.

questions.stem: A 240-W device runs for 10 seconds. Which expression gives the energy used?
options: 2 A × 10 s only
questions.explanation: Electrical energy equals power multiplied by time.

questions.stem: Why is 60-Hz AC particularly relevant to electrical injury in the OR?
options: Less AC than DC is required to provoke ventricular fibrillation
AC cannot pass through capacitive pathways
DC causes fibrillation at roughly one-third the current of AC
AC eliminates impedance from tissue
questions.explanation: The lecture notes that approximately three times more DC than AC is required to cause ventricular fibrillation.

questions.stem: In an AC circuit, resistance alone does not describe opposition to current because capacitance and inductance also contribute. What is the combined quantity?
options: Impedance
Conductance
Capacitance
Power
questions.explanation: Impedance is the total opposition to AC current and includes resistance, capacitance, and inductance.

questions.stem: A capacitor is connected to a DC source and becomes charged. What happens next if no discharge path exists?
options: Current falls after the brief charging period
Current rises continuously
The plates become direct conductors
The insulator converts DC to AC
questions.explanation: A capacitor stores charge on two conductors separated by an insulator. With DC, current flows briefly during charging and then stops without a discharge path.

questions.stem: Which configuration distinguishes OR electrical distribution from typical grounded household power in this lecture?
options: Ungrounded OR power with grounded equipment
Grounded OR power with ungrounded equipment
Both power and equipment intentionally ungrounded
Both configured exactly like household power
questions.explanation: The lecture contrasts grounded household power with an ungrounded OR power system while equipment remains grounded.

questions.stem: The electrosurgical return pad lifts partially from the patient's skin during cautery. What complication becomes more likely?
options: Thermal burn at the reduced contact area
Hypoxic mixture
Hypercarbia from added dead space
Cylinder transfilling
questions.explanation: Reduced return-pad contact concentrates current density and increases burn risk.

questions.stem: Wall power fails and the workstation is running on battery. Which preparations should occur before battery depletion? Select 2.
options: Set up an independent ventilation option such as a Mapleson circuit
Prepare an IV anesthetic technique if volatile delivery becomes unavailable
Increase dependence on electrically powered accessories
Leave the case unchanged until the battery alarm stops
Close the backup O2 cylinder
Disable alarms to conserve power
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends using the battery interval to establish alternative ventilation and an IV anesthetic plan before electrical support is lost.

questions.stem: During airway surgery, which items represent the three sides of the fire triangle? Select 3.
options: Electrocautery
Supplemental O2
Surgical drapes
Scavenging suction
CO2 absorbent
ECG electrodes
questions.explanation: Electrocautery is an ignition source, oxygen is an oxidizer, and drapes are fuel.

questions.stem: Open O2 is being delivered during facial surgery and cautery is about to be used. Which change most directly reduces fire risk?
options: Use the lowest tolerated FiO2 and prevent O2 pooling under drapes
Increase O2 flow immediately before cautery
Seal the drapes around the cannula
Drape before alcohol-based prep is fully dry
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends the lowest tolerated FiO2, avoiding oxygen accumulation, and allowing prep to dry before draping.

questions.stem: A pop and flash are followed by smoke during airway surgery. What should the team assume until proven otherwise?
options: An operating-room fire
Normal cautery artifact
Pipeline crossover
Vaporizer malfunction
questions.explanation: Pop, flash, and smoke are warning signs of fire and require immediate action.

questions.stem: Flame is seen in the endotracheal tube during airway surgery. Which actions should occur simultaneously?
options: Remove the ETT and stop gas flow
Increase O2 and remove the drapes
Close the APL valve and continue ventilation
Disconnect scavenging and increase fresh gas flow
questions.explanation: The lecture's current teaching is to remove the burning tube and stop gas flow simultaneously.

questions.stem: After an airway fire is extinguished and burning material is removed, what is the next priority?
options: Mask ventilate and assess the airway for reintubation or surgical airway
Restart cautery to confirm the source
Discard the ETT and circuit immediately
Increase N2O to reduce FiO2
questions.explanation: After extinguishing the fire, the lecture directs mask ventilation and airway assessment, including possible reintubation or emergency tracheostomy.

questions.stem: A surgical drape ignites on the patient's chest, with no evidence of an airway fire. What is the FIRST response?
options: Stop gases and remove burning drapes/material
Continue ventilation while the surgeon finishes cautery
Leave the drapes in place and assess the airway first
Increase O2 while saline is obtained
questions.explanation: For fire on the patient, the lecture begins with stopping gases and removing the drapes or other burning material.

questions.stem: A fire occurs despite the team identifying the extinguisher during timeout. Which additional action may be required if the room itself is unsafe?
options: Activate the fire response and consider evacuation
Continue the case until the battery fails
Close the scavenger and increase O2
Discard all involved equipment before leaving
questions.explanation: The circulating nurse can activate the fire alarm, and an actual room fire may require evacuation.

questions.stem: After an OR fire is controlled, which actions are appropriate? Select 2.
options: Notify risk management/follow reporting procedures
Preserve the ETT, circuit, drapes, and involved equipment
Discard damaged items before they contaminate the room
Restart the case before documenting the event
Clean the scene before anyone inspects it
Return involved equipment to service immediately
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes formal reporting and preservation of all involved equipment and materials for review.

questions.stem: A provider skips the machine check because another clinician used the workstation earlier. Later a disconnected hose causes hypoxemia. Which prevention principle best fits the lecture?
options: Confirm the pre-use machine check was completed rather than assuming it
Rely on the O2 proportioner to detect disconnected hoses
Leave the backup cylinder open throughout every case
Use pulse oximetry as the substitute for equipment checks
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes confirming the machine check was completed even when tasks are delegated or the machine was previously used.
